samples.question: This image shows five framed rectangular panels of identical size standing side by side in one row, numbered 1 to 5 from left to right. Every panel contains exactly four solid flat glyphs, each printed in its own colour, and all twenty glyphs in the image cover exactly the same amount of area, so ink, size, glyph count and colour carry no information. In every panel the four glyphs come from exactly two outline families, two glyphs from each family, so in every panel some outline shape is repeated. A glyph is only ever printed upright or turned by a quarter, a half or three quarters of a full turn, and it is never mirrored. Two glyphs count as twins only if they have the same outline family and the same turn, so that one of them could be slid over the other and cover it exactly; their colours and their places in the panel never have to agree, and the twins are always printed in two different colours. In exactly one panel a pair of twins is present. In each of the other four panels the two glyphs of each family are turned by different amounts, and no pair of glyphs there could be slid into agreement: at least a fifth of the two glyphs' combined area would still fail to overlap. Which numbered panel contains a pair of twin glyphs, that is two glyphs of the same outline family printed at the same turn? Answer with exactly one of: panel-1, panel-2, panel-3, panel-4, panel-5.
